evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, received 欠部 text
evidence.field: 欠部 entries 欠 and 歌
evidence.text: The received text says 欠 is an open mouth with breath rising out and defines 歌 as 詠也, 从欠哥聲. It assigns 哥 the sound role in this analysis of the received form; it does not establish the earliest graph or explain the ancestry of earlier reported spellings.
evidence.title: 說文解字/08 - 維基文庫

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: Records the Shuowen analysis 从欠、哥聲, also notes a variant 謌 said to use 言, and cites the Shijing line 心之憂矣，我歌且謠 for the sense ‘sing.’ It records praise, song/melody and singable verse as other senses. These citations do not date the composition or a surviving written witness, and their list order does not establish semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 歌 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 歌 character entry; Zhengzhang (2003) reconstruction table
evidence.field: pronunciation comparison: 歌 and 哥
evidence.text: The page groups 歌 and 哥 in Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese phonetic series at *kaːl. This same-system match supports their historical sound relationship, while remaining a reconstruction rather than a directly recorded pronunciation. The page also gives 歌 Baxter–Sagart (2014) *[k]ˤaj; this is a different system and should not be equated with Zhengzhang’s notation.

evidence.field: Baxter–Sagart 2014 table, exact rows 歌 and 欠; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv
evidence.text: The supplied local rows give 歌, Mandarin gē, MC ka, OC *[k]ˤaj, gloss ‘sing, song’; 欠, Mandarin qiàn, MC khjomH, OC *[k]ʰ(r)om-s, gloss ‘yawn’. These exact rows do not establish a phonetic role for 欠; the table contains no supplied row for 哥, so no component-versus-host Baxter–Sagart comparison is made. Unicode character-record URLs were attempted but unavailable through this web tool; these local rows are reported as local data, not externally verified source pages.

evidence.text: Lists standard Mandarin gē (Pinyin), Middle Chinese ka in its romanization, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[k]ˤaj and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *kaːl. These are a present-day reading and modelled historical readings, not direct records of ancient speech.
evidence.title: 歌 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The page reports a late Spring-and-Autumn bronze form associated with 余贎兒鐘 (集成184), a Warring States form, received Shuowen forms and Qin Shuihudi slip evidence. Its account reads the early example as 言+可 and later examples as 欠+哥, with an alternate 言+哥. It is a secondary compilation and its form examples do not establish a continuous lineage, chronological replacement, or whether these are related spellings or variants. The proposed meaning for 哥 is not supported by Shuowen’s phonetic notation.
evidence.title: 歌字形演变字源_汉字「歌」

evidence.text: Cites the Shijing line 我歌且謠 and other classical passages for singing and song-related uses, and records further senses including praise and a bell name. The page’s citations show textual usages but do not by themselves date the graph or establish the order and pathways of semantic change.
evidence.title: 歌 gē - 汉典

evidence.text: Proposes Proto-Sino-Tibetan *gaːr ~ *ga ‘dance; sing; leap; stride’ and compares Burmese က ka ‘dance.’ This is a lexical etymology proposal separate from graph formation. The inspected page does not supply independently checked early Burmese attestations or enough comparative evidence here to establish the cognacy or semantic pathway.

gaps: No primary inscription image or facsimile was inspected. The reported bronze example is secondary evidence only, and sources disagree on its bronze catalogue number (集成184 versus 集成186).

The transition or relationship between reported early 言+可 and received 欠+哥 is unresolved: chronology, variant status, regional spelling, and possible graphic corruption were not decided by the inspected sources. Do not assign origin_form ancestry from these reports alone.
Shuowen supports a semantic-classifier role for 欠 and phonetic role for 哥 in the received form; the text does not establish that this analysis applies to the earliest reported spelling.

The Shijing citation supports textual use of 歌 as ‘sing,’ but no inspected evidence dates the physical witness bearing that graph. No chronology or pathway among sing, song, praise, verse genre and the cited bell name was established.

The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows report 歌 *[k]ˤaj and 欠 *[k]ʰ(r)om-s; no supplied row gives 哥 in that system, so no Baxter–Sagart component-host comparison can be reported. Zhengzhang provides the same-system match 歌/哥 *kaːl.
Current Mandarin local rows are available for 歌 gē, 哥 gē and 欠 qiàn, but official Unicode Unihan character pages could not be inspected in this pass; URLs were attempted and returned internal errors.
The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison with Burmese ka remains unverified through independent comparative or dated Burmese evidence and is separate from graphic formation.
No whole-graph borrowing origin for 歌 is supported. Shuowen’s note concerning spelling with 哥/謌 does not demonstrate that 歌 originated as a whole-character loan.
